podcasts.description:
Rob Snyder is the author of The Power of Pull and writes the newsletter The Physics of Startups. He has advised more than 50 startups on growing from zero to $1 million in ARR, drawing on his own experience as a founder who spent two years pushing a product the market didn’t want before accidentally stumbling onto what actually works. In this episode, we walk step by step through his framework for finding product-market fit, from coming up with an idea to closing your first handful of deals.

We discuss:

1. The PULL framework: Project, Unavoidable, List of options, Limitations

2. Where the best startup ideas come from

3. Tactics for cold outreach and running your first sales call

4. Why Rob advises against design partners

5. Goblin mode: what to do when nothing is working

6. How to apply the PULL framework inside larger companies

podcasts.title: This Is How You Should Actually Make Launch Videos
podcasts.description:
There’s a misconception that a successful launch video needs to cost tens of thousands of dollars and feel like a high-production commercial. But Farza Majeed has a different approach.


Farza is the founder of Clicky and previously built Buildspace, one of the largest online schools for people working on their own ideas. He’s been making videos for over a decade, and today his posts regularly get millions of views. Rather than treating launches as rare, high-stakes moments, he’s made them part of the everyday process of building a company.


Farza sat down with YC’s Aaron Epstein to share his playbook for turning demos into stories people actually want to watch. He breaks down how he scripts videos that still feel off the cuff, why founders should launch constantly, and how to figure out which channels actually convert.

podcasts.title: Democratizing Security for the Agentic Web with Cloudflare CTO Dane Knecht
podcasts.description:
In the transition to the agentic web, security has become an afterthought. Now, organizations are racing to figure out what AI security means, and how to keep their data safe. Live from Cloudflare Connect, Sarah Guo sits down with Cloudflare CTO Dane Knecht to discuss the changing attacker landscape, and how his company is allocating its engineering resources to meet this emerging security challenge. Dane explains how enterprises that have moved away from castle-and-moat infrastructure to more of a zero trust infrastructure for security are in better positions than those who haven’t. He also discusses the challenges of patching 70 years of software and why the software development lifecycle will need to change for security for the agentic web, why he sees token spend in the next 18 months primarily going towards security rather than engineering, how the current web is in a ‘messy middle’ state where humans and agents are riding the same ‘rails’ on the internet, Cloudflare’s conference monetization gateway release as well as its Signals project with OpenAI, the rationale behind the release of Cloudflare OS, and the thinking behind a recent company restructuring. Plus, why Cloudflare hired one thousand interns, and why curiosity about AI is required to be successful at Cloudflare. 



Sign up for new podcasts every week. Email feedback to show@no-priors.com



Follow us on Twitter: @NoPriorsPod | @Saranormous | @EladGil | @Cloudflare | @dok2001

podcasts.title: What will computer chips look like in 2045?
podcasts.description:
I spent two days touring Intel’s most advanced fab and talking to its technical leadership to understand what the chips of the future will look like.

A lot of what's coming next – gate-all-around transistors, backside power, CFET, hybrid bonding – is hard to follow without actually seeing it, so we made all the awesome animated explainers that I wish I had while I was prepping.

I also asked Intel’s leadership how the semiconductor industry will cope with the enormous shock in demand from AI.

AI compute has grown 3x a year for the last decade, but according to Intel's CTO, Intel could only double leading-edge wafer production with today’s global stock of chipmaking tools.

What kinds of tricks can foundries pull to extend this crossover point where demand surges way ahead of supply?

This was a totally new format for us - hope you enjoy!

I also made flashcards for the concepts I had to learn to prep for this episode here.

podcasts.title: Sundar Pichai on Gemini 4 and putting data centers in space
podcasts.description:
Even Google can’t get enough compute. I sit down with Google and Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai shortly after the wider release of Gemini 4 Argon to discuss its early reception, where he still wants the model to improve, and what it takes to keep Google at the frontier of AI.

Pichai explains the recent leadership shakeup at Google DeepMind and why building frontier models has become an “all-consuming” job. We also get into Google’s answer to the personal agent race, how he predicts Gemini will do more work on your behalf, and whether agents will finally bring Search, Gmail, and Gemini together.

I ask him about Google turning free cash flow negative, the risks in the AI infrastructure buildout, and how he plans for demand years before knowing what the models will be capable of. He explains the signals giving him confidence to keep spending and how he uses AI agents to follow model development and compute usage inside Google.

We also discuss Project Suncatcher, Google’s new effort to put AI data centers in space, and why he thinks it belongs alongside bets like Waymo. He shares what’s next for Waymo and Wing, and when he expects quantum computing to become a real business.

Pichai joins Big Technology Podcast to discuss Google's return to the frontier of AI, its strategy for competing with OpenAI, and the enormous computing resources required to build the next generation of models. Tune in to hear why Google is sacrificing short-term Cloud revenue to support AI research, how demand for compute is stretching into 2027, and why its new Gemini 4 Argon model is seeing explosive adoption. We also cover recursive self-improvement, AI agents, the future of Google's products, the possibility of an AI bubble, data centers in space, and Google's partnerships with Apple and Anthropic. Hit play for an in-depth conversation about Google's AI strategy, the fierce competition shaping the industry, and why Pichai believes we're entering a moment of infinite possibilities.

podcasts.title: FULL DISCUSSION: Nvidia Jensen Huang & German Merz Discuss AI, Robotics,Jobs, Germany’s Future |AC1E
podcasts.description:
FULL DISCUSSION: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang joins German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on stage at the Invest in Germany Summit in Berlin for an in-depth discussion about artificial intelligence, industrial transformation, investment, manufacturing and Germany’s position in the global technology race.

Huang explains how AI, digital twins, robotics and autonomous vehicles could reshape factories and industrial production. He argues that Germany can build on its engineering expertise, manufacturing strength and industrial data to develop its own AI capabilities while benefiting from global technology.

The discussion also covers:
- Germany’s AI future: How AI could strengthen German manufacturing and industrial competitiveness.
- Digital twins and smart factories: Why future companies may operate both physical and digital factories.
- AI and employment: Huang’s view that AI can augment specialist knowledge rather than replace deep domain expertise.
- NVIDIA’s investment in Germany: Huang discusses the company’s investments, partnerships and support for German startups.
- AI regulation and safety: Huang outlines the roles of technology, industry best practices and government regulation.
- Europe’s global competitiveness: Merz discusses Germany’s ambitions to become a leading destination for industrial AI.
The conversation highlights the growing importance of AI, robotics, advanced manufacturing and investment as Germany seeks to strengthen its industrial future.

Watch the full discussion from Berlin’s Invest in Germany Summit.

podcasts.title: Ep. 038 - GLM 5.3 on AMD, NVIDIA, and Chinese Chips From Day One (InferenceX) | Kimbo Chen, Wenyao Gao, Jordan Nanos
podcasts.description:
GLM 5.3 only attends to the tokens that matter. It still has to keep every one of them.


Kimbo Chen (@kimbochen) and Wenyao Gao (@gao_wenyao) join Jordan Nanos (@JordanNanos) to dig into AMD catching NVIDIA on InferenceX, how post-training alone pushed an open-weight model within reach of Mythos, and whether Z.ai quietly tuned it for Chinese chips. The team also looks at how GLM 5.3 became a fallback when Claude and GPT refuse security work.
